agent_notes: The Hebrew verse 1 is the superscription; the KJV leaves it unnumbered (30:0) and so the KJV verse numbers run one behind the Hebrew throughout. 'Of David' (ledavid) is read as attribution, not authorship proven; the lamed is ambiguous. 'The house' is unspecified: Rashi and Metzudat David say the Temple, Ibn Ezra prefers David's own cedar house, Malbim reads the body. I kept the Hebrew's bare 'the house'.

Only hodah ('give thanks') is said to repeat hodu of verse 5; the earlier claim that higgid echoes verse 2 is dropped, since verse 2 has no form of the root ngd. 'In my blood': Ibn Ezra and Radak equate blood with life; Metzudat David reads 'when my blood is shed'. I read 'pit' for shachat as my own reading; YLT 'corruption' reflects the other derivation.

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses diliTani as 'drawn up'; I kept it, since the verb is the bucket-from-a-well verb (dalah), and the KJV 'lifted up' loses the image. The final 'li' is rendered 'over me' following Rashi (like 'alay); the plain 'to me' would be the strictly literal sense.

Healing as forgiveness is sourced to Rashi (citing Isaiah 6:10) and Metzudat David ('forgiveness of sin, which is the healing of the soul'); the Targum has only 'you healed me' and is not cited for it. Ibn Ezra and Malbim stress the cry to God alone, not a physician.

agent_notes: Ketiv/Qere: the written form is miyordei ('from those who go down', a participle, cf. Ps 28:1, 143:7), the reading is miyyeredi, an infinitive ('from my going down'). Rashi and Radak read the Qere as an infinitive. The packet glosses the Qere; I follow it in the literal layer and mention the Ketiv in a note. Nephesh is rendered 'my life' in the literal layer and 'my soul' in the drama, where the English is better served by it.

'Weeping' and 'a shout of joy' have no verb or preposition of their own in the second half: 'in the evening it lodges, weeping; and at the morning, a ringing cry'. Ibn Ezra and Meiri note the missing bet ('in weeping', 'in joy'), Meiri comparing 2 Kings 12:11. I follow the plain reading, weeping as the overnight guest. The first half: 'a moment in his anger, life in his favor' is elliptical; the KJV supplied verbs ('endureth', 'is') and the ASV 'a life-time' for chayyim is an interpretation.

agent_notes: 'My mountain' (leharri) is a crux. Ibn Ezra reports three views, among them a yod-suffix reading and one by Judah Halevi. Radak takes the mountain as the intellect, Malbim as the body, Meiri as the soul. I keep 'my mountain' in both layers and leave interpretation to the commentary. Five English versions agree on 'mountain'; they split only on 'made stand strong' (KJV, ASV, Webster) vs. 'kept strong' (BBE).

STEPBible glosses adonai as '[the] Lord' tagged to deity.yhwh; the entity link is as in the packet. The second colon deliberately varies the divine title (YHWH, then Adonai); the packet's KJV text renders both as 'Lord', and the YLT, which gives 'Jehovah' twice, loses the contrast as well.
